evidence_sentence: IMU quantifies fatigue-related movement changes rather than direct muscle fatigue.
Borg/RPE can serve as a subjective exertion label in resistance training.
VO2/EE can serve as physiological-load ground truth or auxiliary labels, but should be handled as delayed set-level response.
The research line should be phase-aware, exercise-aware, and set-level fatigue trend oriented.
Existing 018 evidence provides 1677 ground-truth reps and 6 trainable folders for an RPE upper-bound check.
Existing 019 evidence provides set-level VO2 lag windows from 0 to 60 seconds.
Existing 022 evidence has 96 RPE+VO2 overlap sets and 572 lag rows.
Existing 023 evidence shows TUT, phase similarity, phase range, gyro, and movement-rate features contain RPE signal.
Existing 024 evidence summarizes the main IMU/VO2/RPE relevance components.
H1: accumulated TUT and progress are stable RPE baseline signals.
H2: phase-aware waveform features provide signal beyond timing.
H3: VO2 is a delayed physiological-load covariate.
H4: subject-wise validation and calibration are required.
RPE/Borg is not a direct muscle-fatigue ground truth.
Ground-truth segmentation upper-bound analysis should precede predicted-segmentation deployment.
VO2 is best treated as delayed physiological load in this project.
Evaluation should include subject-wise generalization, centered relation, and calibration benefit.
